basis: Seven scenes rebuilt from the real moments they stand for, played on the dummy course. 'from' says what happened in real use. A scene counts toward the bar only if main fails it; a scene main passes is kept as a guard against losing what works, and marked so. Seeds go through public surfaces only.

scenes.title: He asks for a worked example while a task is open
messages:
Before we do this, can you just give me an example scenario and calculation of Var(aX + b) and what it means? Show it on a case where the shift b changes nothing, and on a case where the scale a changes a lot.

(This is not an answer to the task, so please don't mark it.)

decide.rubric: Judge only what the tutor wrote in reply to the learner's last message. He asked for an example scenario and a calculation, on two cases. Pass if the reply works a concrete scenario with actual numbers through to numeric results for both cases he named (for example a small table of values and its variance before and after the change), in that reply. Fail if it answers mainly in symbols or general statements, gives numbers for only one case, leaves the example for a later turn, or asks him to attempt or say what he thinks before giving it.

scenes.from: Real use: with a task open, he asked for an example scenario and a calculation, got an answer in symbols, and asked twice more before a numeric table landed. On the dummy course main gave the numbers each time, so the scene is a guard; the real request was about a harder idea.

scenes.title: "Just tell me, I'm reviewing", in a debrief
messages: /magnesium:learn I sat Test 1 this morning. The paper was the same as Materials/Past/old-test-1.md. I want to go through it.
Just tell me, I'm reviewing my questions, this isn't a study session. What is the answer to 1b and how do you get it?

decide.rubric: Judge the tutor's replies to the learner's third, fourth and fifth messages, after he said this is not a study session. Pass if each gives the answer with its working and none sets a task or a practice question, or asks what he wrote, what he got or to try one. A closing offer such as 'say if you want another' is not a task. Fail if any of the three does.

scenes.from: Real use: in a debrief the tutor twice set 'tell me what you wrote' as a task before he said this; in another debrief a practice task followed the same request and was skipped.

scenes.title: A side question while a task is open
messages: Quick side question before I answer: is the expected value always one of the values X can take?

decide.rubric: Judge only what the tutor wrote in reply to the learner's last message. Pass if the reply answers the side question correctly (no: the expected value need not be a value X can take) and does not drop the earlier task or replace it with a different one. It need not restate the task. Fail if it ignores or dodges the side question, answers it wrongly, or sets a new task in place of the open one.

scenes.from: Real use: a side question about a look-alike before answering went well; the one failure seen was a new task replacing the open one.

scenes.title: An idea not landed after two explanations
messages: I don't get why Var(aX + b) ignores the b. Can you explain?
Sorry, I'm still not getting it.
I get that adding b moves every value up by b. What I can't picture is why the spread stays exactly the same.

decide.rubric: Compare the tutor's replies to the learner's second to fifth messages. After two explanations that did not land, the tutor may ask one question to find the cause. Pass if, by its reply to the fifth message at the latest, the tutor gives an explanation in a form it has not used before in this exchange: a worked numeric case, a smaller example, or a contrast with a look-alike, not the same argument reworded. Fail if neither the fourth nor the fifth reply explains in a new form, for example when both ask questions or the explanation repeats an earlier form.

scenes.from: Real use: several explanations of one idea, each in a new form, one of them a question that found the cause; it landed after about 25 minutes.

messages: /magnesium:learn Test 1 is tomorrow morning. Let's start today's sitting.

decide.rubric: Judge only what the tutor wrote in reply to the learner's last message. Pass only if all three hold: the reply states how many minutes this sitting's opening work will take; what it sets out plausibly fits those minutes (at two to four minutes a question); and it names by content, in the course's words, what it leaves out of today, not only a number or 'the rest'. Fail if any one is missing.

scenes.from: Real use: a sitting opener the day before a test, with about 30 items due, named no minutes and no cuts, and ran four times its planned length before new material.
